questions.question: Which AWS service is best suited for hosting a static website with only HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and images?

options.text: Amazon EC2
Amazon S3 Static Website Hosting
AWS Lambda
Amazon RDS

explanation.correct: S3 Static Website Hosting is purpose-built for static content — no server management needed.
explanation.why: EC2 requires manual setup and 24x7 costs. Lambda is for serverless compute. RDS is a database.

questions.question: What best defines a static website?

options.text: A website that runs on Python backend
A website with pre-built HTML/CSS/JS files served identically to every visitor
A website hosted on EC2 with Apache
A website with database-driven pages

explanation.correct: Static websites serve the same pre-built files to every visitor — no server-side logic needed.
explanation.why: Options A, C, D describe dynamic website architectures with backend processing.

questions.question: After enabling S3 Static Website Hosting and disabling Block Public Access, a user still gets 403. What is missing?

options.text: EC2 instance needs to be started
CloudFront distribution is not deployed
A bucket policy granting s3:GetObject to Principal * has not been added
The S3 bucket name is not globally unique

explanation.correct: Two steps are required for public access: (1) disable Block Public Access AND (2) add a bucket policy with s3:GetObject for Principal *.
explanation.why: Disabling Block Public Access alone is not enough. The bucket policy must explicitly allow public reads.

questions.question: Which S3 action grants users permission to read and download objects from a bucket?

options.text: s3:PutObject
s3:DeleteObject
s3:GetObject
s3:ListBucket

explanation.correct: s3:GetObject grants permission to read and download objects from an S3 bucket.
explanation.why: PutObject is for uploading, DeleteObject for deleting, ListBucket for listing keys — not for object downloads.

questions.question: What does CDN stand for?

options.text: Cloud Delivery Node
Content Distribution Network
Content Delivery Network
Central Data Network

explanation.correct: CDN stands for Content Delivery Network — a globally distributed network of servers that deliver internet content faster.
explanation.why: The other options are incorrect expansions of the acronym.

questions.question: What are the mini-servers in a CDN network called?

options.text: Availability Zones
Regions
Edge Locations (also called Points of Presence)
Subnets

explanation.correct: CDN mini data centers are called edge locations, also known as Points of Presence (PoP). They cache content near users.
explanation.why: Availability Zones and Regions are AWS infrastructure concepts for compute/storage, not CDN caching.

questions.question: What is Amazon CloudFront?

options.text: A relational database service
A static file storage service
AWS managed Content Delivery Network (CDN) service
A load balancing service

explanation.correct: Amazon CloudFront is AWS's CDN service. It delivers content with low latency using a global network of edge locations.
explanation.why: S3 is for storage, RDS for databases, ALB for load balancing. CloudFront is specifically the CDN.

questions.question: What must you specify as the Index Document when enabling S3 Static Website Hosting?

options.text: The bucket ARN
The filename of your main landing page (e.g., index.html)
The CloudFront distribution ID
The IAM role name

explanation.correct: The Index document is the filename of your main landing page and must match exactly (e.g., index.html).
explanation.why: S3 needs to know which file to serve when a user visits the website root URL.

questions.question: What Principal value in a bucket policy grants public internet access to everyone?

options.text: Principal: aws
Principal: public
Principal: *
Principal: arn:aws:s3:::*

explanation.correct: The wildcard asterisk (*) in Principal means everyone on the internet can access the specified resources.
explanation.why: The other values are not valid formats for granting public access.

questions.question: Why does an S3 bucket in Mumbai cause high latency for users in Germany?

options.text: S3 buckets cannot serve international traffic
The request and response must travel thousands of kilometers, increasing round-trip time
Germany is not an AWS-supported region
S3 does not support HTTPS for international connections

explanation.correct: Geographic distance increases network round-trip time. A user in Germany waiting for a response from Mumbai experiences high latency due to the physical distance.
explanation.why: S3 supports international traffic but the single-region deployment causes latency for distant users.

questions.question: What is OAC in Amazon CloudFront?

options.text: Object Access Certificate
Origin Access Control — allows CloudFront to access a private S3 bucket without making it public
Open Authentication Configuration
Outbound Access Control

explanation.correct: OAC (Origin Access Control) is a CloudFront feature that gives CloudFront permission to access a private S3 bucket securely.
explanation.why: The other options are not valid AWS terms.

questions.question: When setting the origin for CloudFront with an S3 static website, what should you select as the origin?

options.text: The S3 static website endpoint URL
The S3 bucket name
The EC2 public IP
The CloudFront ARN

explanation.correct: Use the S3 bucket name as the origin. The website endpoint URL requires a public bucket and cannot be used with OAC.
explanation.why: Using the bucket name allows OAC, keeping the bucket private while CloudFront accesses it securely.

questions.question: What are the THREE key settings when creating a CloudFront distribution for an S3 static website?

options.text: Region, AMI, and Security Group
Origin (S3 bucket name), OAC (Origin Access Control), and Default Root Object (index.html)
VPC, Subnet, and IAM Role
Load Balancer, Target Group, and Health Check

explanation.correct: The three essential settings are: Origin (S3 bucket name), OAC (for private bucket access), and Default Root Object (index.html for the homepage).
explanation.why: The other options relate to EC2/networking setup, not CloudFront.

questions.question: After enabling OAC in CloudFront, what does CloudFront automatically do to the S3 bucket?

options.text: Makes the bucket publicly accessible
Deletes all existing bucket policies
Generates a bucket policy allowing only that specific CloudFront distribution to read objects
Replicates the bucket to all AWS regions

explanation.correct: CloudFront auto-generates a bucket policy that allows only cloudfront.amazonaws.com from your specific account and distribution ID. The bucket stays private.
explanation.why: OAC creates a controlled, private access path — it does not make the bucket public.

questions.question: What is TTL in CDN caching?

options.text: Total Transfer Limit
Time to Live — how long an edge location keeps cached content before refreshing from origin
Token to Login
Traffic Throttle Level

explanation.correct: TTL (Time to Live) defines how long a cached object stays in an edge location before it checks the origin for updates.
explanation.why: Short TTL gives fresher content but more origin hits. Long TTL maximizes caching efficiency.

questions.question: A user requests a file from a CloudFront edge location that has never cached it before. What happens?

options.text: Cache hit — file served instantly from edge
Cache miss — edge fetches from origin, caches it, then serves the user
Request is rejected as unauthorized
File is served directly from EC2

explanation.correct: The first request to an uncached edge location is a cache miss. The edge fetches from origin, stores a copy, and serves the user. Future requests from that region are cache hits.
explanation.why: Cache hits require content to already be cached. First-time requests always trigger a cache miss.

questions.question: Which of the following can serve as an origin for CloudFront?

options.text: Only Amazon S3 buckets
Amazon S3 and Application Load Balancers
Only EC2 instances
Amazon RDS databases

explanation.correct: CloudFront supports multiple origin types: S3 buckets, Application Load Balancers, EC2 instances, API Gateway, and custom HTTP servers.
explanation.why: RDS is a database and cannot be a CloudFront origin. CloudFront is not limited to S3.

questions.question: What is the key difference between an edge location and an AWS Availability Zone?

options.text: They are the same thing
Edge locations are full data centers; AZs are caching nodes
Edge locations are CDN caching mini-servers; AZs are isolated data center clusters within a Region for compute and storage
AZs are used by CloudFront; edge locations are used by EC2

explanation.correct: Edge locations are small caching nodes for CloudFront CDN delivery. AZs are full data center clusters within AWS Regions hosting EC2, RDS, and other services.
explanation.why: These are distinct infrastructure concepts — edge locations are CDN-specific, not general compute resources.

questions.question: Security team flags the S3 website bucket as publicly accessible. Customers must still access the website. What is the best solution?

options.text: Move to EC2 and open port 80
Create a CloudFront distribution with OAC — keep bucket private, serve via CloudFront URL
Enable MFA on the S3 bucket
Remove static website hosting entirely

explanation.correct: CloudFront + OAC is the correct solution: bucket stays private, only CloudFront can access it via OAC, and customers use the CloudFront URL for global, low-latency access.
explanation.why: Moving to EC2 is unnecessary overhead for static content. MFA is not relevant here. Removing hosting breaks the site.

questions.question: You updated S3 files but CloudFront users still see old content. What is the cause and fix?

options.text: S3 bucket needs to be made public again
Edge locations are serving cached content — wait for TTL or create a CloudFront cache invalidation
Delete and recreate the CloudFront distribution
Update Route 53 DNS records

explanation.correct: Edge locations serve cached copies until TTL expires. Create a cache invalidation in CloudFront to force edge locations to immediately fetch fresh content from origin.
explanation.why: This is expected CDN caching behavior. Cache invalidation is the proper tool for urgent updates.

questions.question: What is a critical requirement for the S3 static website endpoint URL to work?

options.text: A VPC endpoint must be configured
Block Public Access must be disabled AND a bucket policy must grant s3:GetObject to Principal *
A CloudFront distribution must be in place
EC2 must be running in the same region

explanation.correct: The S3 website endpoint requires both steps: Block Public Access disabled AND a bucket policy granting public read access. Without both, users get 403 Forbidden.
explanation.why: These are two separate requirements — missing either one causes access failure.

questions.question: What does the condition block in an OAC bucket policy specify?

options.text: The IP address range of allowed users
The specific AWS account ID and CloudFront distribution ARN allowed to access the bucket
The S3 bucket region
The IAM user who can access the bucket

explanation.correct: The OAC bucket policy condition includes AWS:SourceAccount (your account ID) and AWS:SourceArn (your distribution ARN), ensuring only your specific distribution can access the bucket.
explanation.why: This prevents other CloudFront distributions from other AWS accounts from accessing your private bucket.

questions.question: Users in Asia report a static website hosted in us-east-1 S3 loads in 8-10 seconds. The company needs sub-second performance globally. Best architecture?

options.text: Create S3 buckets in every region and replicate content
Move to EC2 with Auto Scaling Group
Place a CloudFront distribution in front of S3 — edge locations near Asia cache and serve content
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration

explanation.correct: CloudFront is optimal. Edge locations near Asia cache the content after the first request, delivering sub-second performance without duplicating buckets or adding compute.
explanation.why: Multi-bucket replication is complex and expensive. EC2 adds overhead for static content. Transfer Acceleration improves uploads to S3, not delivery to end users.

questions.question: A developer deletes the OAC-generated bucket policy from S3. What is the immediate consequence?

options.text: The S3 bucket becomes publicly accessible
CloudFront cannot access S3 objects — all users get errors through CloudFront
CloudFront auto-regenerates the policy
EC2 stops serving traffic

explanation.correct: Without the OAC bucket policy, CloudFront loses permission to read from the private S3 bucket. All CloudFront requests fail with access denied. The bucket itself remains private.
explanation.why: The OAC policy is the authorization bridge between CloudFront and S3. Removing it breaks access for all users.

questions.question: Which statement about OAC vs OAI (Origin Access Identity) is correct per current AWS recommendations?

options.text: OAI is newer and recommended; OAC is deprecated
Both are equally recommended
OAC is current recommended approach; OAI is legacy. OAC supports SSE-KMS encrypted S3 which OAI does not
OAI is required for private buckets; OAC is for public buckets

explanation.correct: AWS recommends OAC over OAI. OAC provides better security and supports SSE-KMS encrypted S3 buckets — a key limitation of the older OAI.
explanation.why: AWS is moving OAC as the standard. OAI still works but lacks support for newer encryption features.

questions.question: A website must show different content for each logged-in user based on their account data in a database. Can S3 Static Website Hosting handle this?

options.text: Yes — enable static hosting and upload personalized pages
No — per-user dynamic content requires a backend server; S3 only serves static pre-built files
Yes — S3 can run Node.js backend
Yes — use S3 with RDS to generate pages

explanation.correct: S3 only serves static pre-built files. Per-user content from a database requires a compute service like EC2, Lambda, or Elastic Beanstalk.
explanation.why: S3 cannot execute server-side code. Dynamic content generation requires a running compute environment.

questions.question: A CloudFront distribution has S3 in Mumbai as origin. A Canadian user requests a file. The Canadian edge location has no cache. What happens?

options.text: Request is rejected with 503
Canadian edge fetches from Mumbai S3, caches it, serves the user — future Canadian requests served from cache
Request redirects to nearest AWS region
User is forced to access Mumbai S3 URL directly

explanation.correct: On cache miss, the edge fetches from origin (S3 Mumbai), stores a cached copy per TTL settings, and serves it. Subsequent Canadian users get it from the local edge cache.
explanation.why: This is core CDN cache miss behavior — first request populates the cache, subsequent requests are served locally.

questions.question: Which Resource value in an S3 bucket policy correctly grants access to ALL objects inside a bucket?

options.text: arn:aws:s3:::bucket-name (no wildcard — applies to bucket itself only)
arn:aws:s3:::bucket-name/* (/* means all objects inside the bucket)
* (grants access to all S3 buckets in the account)
arn:aws:iam:::bucket-name/*

explanation.correct: arn:aws:s3:::bucket-name/* is correct. The /* wildcard means all objects within the bucket. Without /*, the policy applies to the bucket itself (for listing operations), not the files inside.
explanation.why: Omitting /* is a very common mistake — GetObject access requires the /* wildcard to cover all objects.

questions.question: CloudFront TTL is 86400 seconds. A critical website update was made 1 hour ago but users see old content. What is the fastest fix?

options.text: Wait 23 hours for TTL to expire naturally
Delete and recreate the CloudFront distribution
Create a CloudFront cache invalidation to force edge locations to fetch fresh content immediately
Change the S3 bucket to public

explanation.correct: Cache invalidation instructs CloudFront edge locations to discard cached copies and fetch fresh content from origin on the next request — without waiting for TTL.
explanation.why: Waiting is unacceptable for urgent updates. Deleting the distribution is destructive and unnecessary.

questions.question: What is the key difference between S3 Transfer Acceleration and CloudFront?

options.text: They are the same service
S3 Transfer Acceleration speeds up uploads from users to S3; CloudFront speeds up content delivery from AWS to users
CloudFront is only for S3; Transfer Acceleration works with all AWS services
Transfer Acceleration caches at edge locations; CloudFront does not

explanation.correct: S3 Transfer Acceleration uses edge locations to accelerate uploads to S3. CloudFront caches at edge locations to accelerate downloads to users. They optimize opposite directions of data flow.
explanation.why: For serving a website to users, CloudFront is correct. Transfer Acceleration helps when users upload large files to S3.
